body_markdown:
- Proposed all-share acquisition would extend Turbo Energy’s reach across the energy project lifecycle, connecting solar infrastructure, battery storage, intelligent energy management and ongoing services.


- Expanded platform would strengthen Turbo Energy’s growing commercial and industrial focus, creating opportunities for broader project revenue and long-term customer relationships.


***VALENCIA, Spain*** ***— (GLOBE NEWSWIRE)*** ***—*** ***November 17*** ***,*** ***2026 —*** Turbo Energy, S.A. (Nasdaq: TURB) (“Turbo Energy” or the “Company”), a global technology integrator specializing in AI-driven storage and energy management solutions, today announced a proposed acquisition that would mark a defining step in its development as an integrated energy technology platform. The transaction would position Turbo Energy to take a broader role in how customers develop, operate and expand their energy infrastructure, connecting solar generation, battery storage, proprietary energy management software and lifecycle services.


The proposed all-share transaction would bring IM2 Energía Solar, S.L.U. (“IM2”), a solar project development, engineering and construction business, and Greentech Solutions, S.L. (“Greentech”), an operations and maintenance business, into the Turbo Energy group. Both companies are currently wholly owned by Umbrella Global Energy, S.A. (“Umbrella”), Turbo Energy’s majority shareholder. The transaction was reviewed and approved by a special committee of independent directors of Turbo Energy’s Board of Directors, which received an independent valuation analysis and fairness opinion. Completion remains subject to shareholder approvals and other applicable requirements.


The expanded platform would support Turbo Energy’s ambition to become a long-term energy partner for commercial and industrial customers, while retaining its established residential and small commercial business.


**An Integrated Technology Platform Across the Energy Project Lifecycle**


The proposed integration would unite three complementary capabilities within a single platform, connecting the development and delivery of energy infrastructure with intelligent control and long-term asset performance:


- **Energy Project Development and Delivery:** assessment, design, permitting, engineering, construction and commissioning of integrated solar-plus-storage projects, incorporating energy management requirements from the outset.
- **Storage and Intelligent Energy Management** : battery storage integration, power conversion, controls and Turbo Energy’s proprietary energy management software to coordinate solar generation, storage, grid interaction and customer demand.
- **Operations and Lifecycle Services:** monitoring, preventive and corrective maintenance and asset performance management, complemented by opportunities for software updates, energy management optimization, capacity expansions, equipment upgrades and repowering.


Together, these capabilities would position Turbo Energy to deliver and manage more complete energy systems. By connecting project engineering and ongoing operations with its proprietary energy management software, the Company would seek to create additional opportunities to deploy and optimize its technology across new and existing customer installations.


As industry context, in its 2023 analysis, McKinsey & Company estimated that the global battery energy storage systems market could reach $120 billion to $150 billion by 2030, with commercial and industrial installations projected to grow at approximately 13% annually, reaching 52–70 GWh of annual additions by 2030. \[1\]


**Expanding Revenue Opportunities Across the Customer Relationship**


The proposed acquisition would broaden the scope of business Turbo Energy can pursue within each customer relationship. Alongside storage systems and energy management technology, the expanded platform would be able to offer project development, engineering, construction and ongoing services, including maintenance of energy installations, software updates and energy management optimization, increasing its potential participation in customer energy investments.


The integration would also create opportunities to introduce battery storage and intelligent energy management across IM2’s and Greentech’s existing customer installations, while offering solar solutions, engineering and maintenance services to Turbo Energy customers, including solar generation associated with storage projects.


Beyond initial project delivery, the platform would be positioned to pursue maintenance contracts, system optimization, capacity expansions and equipment upgrades throughout the operating life of the installed base.


“Our ambition is to build an energy technology platform that helps customers take greater control of how they generate, store and use energy,” said **Mariano Soria, Chief Executive Officer of Turbo Energy** . “This proposed acquisition is intended to advance that vision, giving Turbo Energy a broader platform to deliver integrated energy systems and manage their performance over time, as we seek to become a long-term energy partner for commercial and industrial customers.”


**Transaction Structure and Ownership**


Under the proposed transaction, Umbrella would contribute its entire equity interests in IM2 and Greentech to Turbo Energy in exchange for 39,501,491 newly issued Turbo Energy ordinary shares, for an aggregate issue amount of €9,271,000, including nominal value and share premium.


The consideration would consist entirely of newly issued shares, with no cash payment to Umbrella and no cash proceeds to Turbo Energy. Upon completion, IM2 and Greentech would become directly wholly owned subsidiaries of Turbo Energy.


Based on 66,522,215 ordinary shares outstanding as of November 16, 2026, and assuming no other changes to the Company’s issued share capital before completion, the new shares would represent approximately 37.26% of Turbo Energy’s ordinary share capital immediately following the issuance. Umbrella’s resulting ownership would be approximately 76.48%.


The securities to be issued are ordinary shares, not American Depositary Shares (“ADSs”). At the current ratio of five ordinary shares per ADS, the proposed issuance would represent approximately 7.90 million ADSs on an equivalent basis.


**Related-Party Transaction and Shareholder Approvals**


The proposed acquisition is a related-party transaction because Umbrella is Turbo Energy’s majority shareholder and currently owns 100% of IM2 and Greentech.


The proposed transaction will be submitted to shareholders at Turbo Energy’s Extraordinary General Meeting on December 14, 2026. Umbrella has also convened an Extraordinary General Meeting for that date.


Completion remains subject to approval by the shareholders of both companies and the satisfaction of the remaining applicable corporate, contractual and regulatory requirements, including the formal contribution of IM2 and Greentech and the issuance and subscription of the new Turbo Energy ordinary shares.
